Isolated full dev-environment stack per worktree with port checkout

From a small Coastfile, each git worktree gets its own containerized copy of the app's services and volumes on dynamic ports, so parallel agents never collide; one instance at a time is 'checked out' onto the canonical host ports, and shared service groups can be reused across instances.
Red/green review of agent edits inside a rendered document
Agent edits to a markdown file show as red/green changes inside the WYSIWYG (Lexical) editor, matched by tree diff, and you accept or reject each change in place instead of reading a text diff.
Deterministic AI-slop detector for generated code

Regex and AST analyzers flag typical AI-generated leftovers (placeholder comments, debug prints, over-defensive code, stale TODOs, excessive docs) before review, with suppression and auto-fix, so cleanup costs no tokens.
Prompt-to-app builder with instant previews and runtime-error repair

The agent asks clarifying questions, writes a full-stack app, bundles it into an instantly served preview (no dev server), captures the browser console of the preview, repairs runtime errors and redeploys, with a pre-deploy safety gate and restore points.
Agent overlay on the owner's own shell

The owner's normal shell runs inside a PTY wrapper; a hotkey opens the agent CLI as an overlay that can read the visible screen and scrollback after pattern-based privacy filtering, get cwd/shell context updates, and queue exact input that is typed only after the owner approves.
AI readiness score for a project
Scores how ready a repository is for coding agents (instruction files for Claude, Codex and Gemini, context size, custom extensions) and offers one-click fixes.
Guard plugin forcing headless Claude Code to end with final JSON

An embedded Claude Code plugin with hooks that blocks commit/push 'finalizer' commands inside the executor and refuses to stop until the run emits the required final JSON, so the runtime (not the model) owns commit and handoff.
Rendered UI evidence gate (render, score, revise)

After an agent builds a screen, the UI is rendered and checked by deterministic, code, visual and temporal reports against JSON schemas; an evidence gate blocks acceptance until the reports pass, and the agent revises.
Project design-rule compiler and semantic palette generator
Compiles chosen design decisions into project-local rules, generates semantic palettes and spacing contracts, and keeps the project's existing choices across updates.
Repository docs kept in sync with code changes

Builds a tree of every class and function with its callers and callees, writes documentation for each in dependency order, and on each commit detects changed objects through git and regenerates only their docs (usable as a pre-commit hook).
Repository wiki with evidence-grounded claims and targeted updates

The agent writes a linked Markdown wiki of a repository where each fact is stored as a claim pointing at versioned source evidence; on later runs only claims whose evidence changed are revisited, links are validated, finished pages survive interruption, and related repos' wikis can be searched together over MCP.
Expedited human review cards with diff image and voting

When a change is ready, a review card with a rendered diff image is posted to Slack or the author's DM; eligible people vote, readiness and eligibility are checked, and the change merges once approved.
Fetch a dependency's source at the installed version

The agent asks for a package (npm, PyPI, crates.io or a GitHub repo); the tool resolves the version actually in the lockfile, fetches that version's source into a cache and returns its path so the agent can grep and read the real code.
Compile, deploy and verify smart contracts from chat

The agent writes Solidity, compiles it with solc, deploys to a chosen EVM chain (server key or the user's wallet), records only after a successful creation receipt, and verifies source on Etherscan or Blockscout.
Hardware project designer (OpenSCAD and parts inventory)

From a plain description, extracts requirements, picks components (checking a stored parts inventory first), designs the circuit and writes an OpenSCAD enclosure, validating it and exporting STL plus a preview image.
Design handoff reader for coding agents

Pulls requirement pages (Axure text, annotations, focused crops by text, block id or coordinates) and design drafts from a design-handoff service, downloads semantically named slices and extracts sizes, spacing, colours and fonts with an HTML+CSS reference for the agent to adapt.
Team lessons turned into deterministic commit-blocking checks

Repo-specific team knowledge is stored as reviewable memory and briefed to the agent before it acts; each hard-won lesson becomes a deterministic anti-pattern/precommit check that refuses the commit (not another model opinion) when the code repeats a known mistake, with a verdict and precision gate.

The agent resolves a library name to an id and pulls current, version-specific documentation and code examples for it into context, as an MCP server, AI SDK tools or a CLI plus skill, so it stops inventing outdated APIs.
Pinned coding-agent runtimes installed into agent workspaces
A release catalog with cache installs pinned builds of Claude Code, Codex and Node into each agent's workspace so hosted coding agents run inside the agent's own computer.
Evolutionary code optimization (MAP-Elites islands + evaluator cascade)

Give it a program and a scoring script; it repeatedly asks models for diffs or rewrites, runs a staged evaluator with timeouts, keeps a MAP-Elites archive across migrating islands, and checkpoints/resumes, so the user gets a measurably better version of a function, prompt or kernel; includes a web visualizer of the program lineage.
Coding agents in remote sandboxes over one HTTP API

A static binary inside any sandbox (E2B, Daytona, Modal, Docker, Cloudflare, Vercel and more) runs the chosen coding agent and exposes sessions, permissions and streamed events over HTTP/SSE in one universal event schema, with transcript persistence adapters (SQLite, Postgres, IndexedDB) for later replay.
Working / blocked / idle detection for any terminal coding agent

Per-agent detection manifests (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Gemini, Hermes and 20 more) read each terminal pane and mark it working, blocked or idle, so the owner sees which agent needs an answer and agents can wait until another agent is truly blocked.
Mixed coding-agent task plans landed in plan order

A read-only planner researches the repo, asks about vague points and returns a task graph where each task names its coding agent, model, effort and mode; the owner edits it before anything runs, independent tasks run in parallel worktrees, completion is decided by a marker in the runner's output, and passing work lands on one integration branch in plan order.
Bridge from the running app into the coding agent
A local bridge streams errors, console output and screenshots from the app being developed into the agent session and lets the agent send control back, Sentry-style, with an MCP server.

Each change gets a folder with proposal, delta specs (ADDED/MODIFIED/REMOVED requirements with WHEN/THEN scenarios), design and tasks; an artifact graph says what comes next, a validator checks scenarios and task lists, and archive merges the deltas into the living specs.
Co-edit guard for blocks that must change together

Tag a code block and the doc or config it affects; on a diff the check reports any block edited without its partner, compares values across files, and runs keep-sorted/unique/pattern and AI-written checks, so an agent's edits do not leave docs stale.
Dependency API changes since the model's training cutoff

Reads the project's lockfiles, finds which pinned Python packages changed after the coding model's cutoff, statically diffs their APIs, shows where the code uses changed APIs, and writes short AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md notes so the agent avoids the old form, with no model calls.

Builds a whole app from a description: a spec writer clarifies requirements, an architect picks stack and templates, a tech lead splits epics into tasks, and developer/code-monkey agents implement each task with the user reviewing between steps.
Lists every localhost port that each agent's process tree is listening on (dev servers it started), with the owning pane, and can terminate the process holding a port.
Use a GitHub repository as a tool for a task

Describe a task; the agent searches and filters GitHub for a suitable repo, ranks its important files, summarizes how to use it, then installs and runs it in Docker (repairing pip errors) to produce the result.
Open a project in its dev container
Parses devcontainer.json, resolves Dev Container features from OCI registries and builds/starts the container with Docker so the project can be opened inside its declared environment.
Diff coverage gate and patch ratchet
CI gates that fail a change when lines it touched are not covered by tests, and a ratchet baseline that only lets quality numbers improve, so agent-written patches cannot lower coverage.
Block secrets from entering git in agent commits

Before an agent's git commit or push runs, staged added lines are scanned with gitleaks and the command is blocked on a secret; --no-verify and --no-gpg-sign are refused, reads of protected paths are denied, and a native pre-commit hook plus CI action act as backstops.
One approval inbox for external coding-agent CLIs

Installs hook scripts into Claude Code, Codex, Grok, pi and others so their permission prompts and questions arrive as notification-style banners in one panel, answered with a primary action or options, with remembered per-agent approvals.
Performance investigation workflow with baselines and profilers

A structured perf investigation keeps state across sessions: it records baselines, runs benchmarks, finds the breaking point under load, profiles Node, Python, Go, Java and Rust code, tracks hypotheses as experiments, and compares results to the stored baseline before accepting an optimisation.

Work items move through Ideation, Refinement, Spec, Sprint and Tasks only along allowed transitions; moving forward requires recorded evidence (linked tests, coverage, smoke and delivery evidence) or an explicit, visible skip, and ambiguity checks gate ideas and refinements.
Terminal sessions that survive app quit and SSH drops (zmx)

Every terminal runs inside a small session daemon rather than as a child of the app, so quitting, relaunching or losing an SSH link reattaches each session with its scrollback instead of restarting it.
Compact build and test output wrappers
Wrappers run Maven, npm/Node and Go test commands and print only failures, counts and the lines needed to fix them, cutting output by up to 99% so agents keep context for the actual work.
The agent can offload a build/compile to another host, syncing sources and returning results, so heavy compilation runs off the local machine.
Design agent with side-by-side mockup variants on a canvas

From one prompt the agent writes several HTML/CSS mockup variants and a theme (palette, fonts) into a design folder; a canvas view shows them side by side to compare, fork and iterate, then the chosen design can be handed to a coding agent.
Compare two review runs: new, persisting, resolved, not re-checked

After fixing code, re-run the review and see which findings are new, which persist (with updated line numbers), which are resolved, and which were never re-checked, following renamed files; shown in a local web viewer.
Drive Electron desktop apps (Slack and others) over CDP

Electron apps such as Slack are relaunched with a debugging port, show an overlay inviting them to join the agent's session, and are then controlled through the same DevTools protocol as browser tabs, so the agent reads and acts in desktop apps by DOM instead of pixels.
Learn an app by exploring, then use the learned guide

Before doing real tasks the agent explores an app on its own (or watches a human demo) and writes a short document per UI element describing what it does; at task time those per-app docs are fed to the model so it taps the right controls.
Critic-checked desktop steps (planner critic, step check, actor critic)

Before each planned step a step-check model looks at the live screen and decides whether the step is already done, needs changing or should run; after acting an actor critic verifies the result and corrects it, and a planner critic revises the plan, so tasks work from any starting state.
Global kill-switch hotkey with heartbeat that must be live before any input

A registered global hotkey chord latches a stop of all agent desktop input; the listener heartbeats to a supervisor and input is refused when no stop path is live or its heartbeat is stale, until the user explicitly resets.
Self-evolving phone agent with learned tips and shortcuts

A manager/operator/reflector/notetaker team runs phone tasks over ADB; after each task experience reflectors write general tips and reusable multi-step shortcuts to a long-term store that later tasks load, so the agent gets faster and more reliable with use.
iOS Simulator streamed into the app window

The iOS Simulator's framebuffer is streamed into a pane next to the chat, so the agent and owner can see and interact with the app being built without switching windows; simulator targets are enumerated and picked per chat.
Persistent agent VM with incremental snapshot and state reconcile

Each agent gets its own lightweight VM that boots fast and, unlike a disposable sandbox, keeps its filesystem and memory between sessions via incremental QEMU snapshots and a state-reconcile step, so an agent's computer can be paused and resumed with everything intact.
Self-hosted microVM sandboxes with snapshot, clone and rollback

Run agent sandboxes as hardware-isolated KVM microVMs on your own machines (sub-60ms start, E2B SDK compatible), with copy-on-write snapshots to clone a sandbox, roll back to any saved state, and pause on one node and resume on another.
Wake a sleeping computer before connecting
Sends a Wake-on-LAN magic packet to the owner's computer so a remote session can start even when the machine is asleep.
Attach to existing tmux, zellij and screen sessions from the browser

Lists the user's running tmux/zellij/screen sessions, windows and panes and attaches to them in a web terminal, so an agent started in a terminal earlier can be picked up and steered from the phone; a 'vt' wrapper forwards any new terminal command too.
WSL-to-Windows screen capture with region masking

A pi extension lets a WSL-hosted agent capture the Windows desktop (full, region, monitor, active or a specific window) using only built-in powershell.exe + .NET; window mode uses PrintWindow PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT to grab even occluded windows, and regions can be cropped, resized and masked to hide sensitive pixels before sharing.
Privacy screen masks the physical display during remote control

While someone controls the computer remotely, the local monitors are covered by masks excluded from capture; touching local input asks to disconnect and locks the session (macOS, Windows, Hyprland gate).
Shared PTY where the AI co-types in the human's live terminal

The agent and the person share one live PTY (local, SSH or Docker): the AI types its commands straight into the same interactive terminal the human is watching and can type in, rather than running commands in a hidden shell, with a PTY manager and agent-event stream keeping both sides in sync.
Drive desktop apps through their scripting runtimes

The agent sends a script through one shell command; a COM, AppleScript or local-HTTP bridge runs it inside Photoshop, Illustrator, Premiere, After Effects, Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Blender, Houdini, 3ds Max or Unity and returns JSON, with per-app API indexes and guides, no screenshots or MCP server.

When switched on, the app captures the screen every N minutes, asks the model for the single best next step grounded in what is visible, and shows it as a suggestion card that only prefills the message box when clicked; screenshots are deleted and never persisted.
Disposable real VMs with operator-approved egress

An agent creates, uses and recreates full Linux VMs from digest-pinned golden images through one constrained socket API; guests reach only a package cache and configured mock ports, and any other destination becomes an egress request the operator approves.
Synology NAS file, sharing and transfer tools
The agent can discover a Synology NAS, keep per-NAS profiles, list/upload/download/move files, create share links and run transfers through DSM APIs, also exposed as a `co syno` CLI and skill.
Agent-native email over JMAP with proof-of-work auth

A JMAP email client built for agents (send, reply with context, blob upload with limits, charset handling) authenticated by client-computed proof-of-work, exposed as MCP tools and an n8n node, so an agent operates its own inbox autonomously.

Checks every open PR the owner has on GitHub, sorts them into needs-you versus waiting-on-others, analyses CI failures and maintainer comments, drafts replies and rebases for approval, grades new issues to pick up, and checks a repo's policy on AI contributions first.
Natural-language robot control skills over MCP

An agent commands physical robots (Unitree Go2/G1, arms, MAVLink drones) through skills such as navigate to a semantic place, follow a person, observe, GPS travel points and stop, exposed over an MCP server so outside agents can drive them.
MCP aggregating proxy with per-user access and downstream token refresh

One MCP endpoint fronts many downstream MCP servers, pooling their connections and refreshing each server's own OAuth tokens, and exposes to each caller only the slice of tools/skills their identity is allowed, so the agent never holds the downstream credentials.

Ready tool servers for ServiceNow, Zendesk, Gong, Salesloft, Ashby, Vanta, Freshservice, Statuspage, Productboard, Monday, HubSpot and Salesforce so an agent can read and act in common sales, support, HR and compliance systems.

Agent channels and tickets are mirrored to a GitHub Projects v2 board: channels become epics, tickets become draft items, and Type/Status/Priority custom fields stay in sync while the app stays the source of truth.

A single provider interface lists and imports tickets from GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Asana, Trello, Notion, Plane, Monday, Featurebase, Forgejo, Plain and YouTrack so any ticket can be sent to an agent task.
Support-inbox autopilot with sentiment x urgency routing
Each incoming email is classified (intent, sentiment level, urgency 1-5) and a decision matrix routes it to auto-send, a human-review draft queue, or escalation with SLA timers and IM notifications.
Email triage that learns importance, with ready reply drafts

The built-in mail client classifies threads into important and everything else (and labels), learns from the user's importance and category corrections, and pre-drafts replies to important mail using the knowledge graph.
Desktop Outlook through COM (no cloud sign-in)

On Windows, the agent reads, searches, drafts and sends mail and reads the calendar through the locally installed Outlook client over COM, returning structured JSON, so no Microsoft Graph app registration or OAuth is needed.
Read and write Microsoft OneNote notebooks, sections and pages through Microsoft Graph with the owner's signed-in account.
Agent Bitcoin wallet with local spend policy and L402

An agent holds an encrypted-seed Bitcoin L2 wallet to send, receive and pay Lightning invoices and L402 API paywalls, bounded by a local spend ledger, recipient allowlist, fee guards and a policy bound to the seed; secrets are never printed.
Signs in to Tesla Fleet API with OAuth and lets the agent read vehicle data and location and send commands such as charging, climate and locks.
Agent tools for Hikvision, Axis and Vivotek IP cameras/DVRs plus Ring and Blink: device info, snapshots, live stream, motion detection settings, events and recordings.
Ask a connected SQL or graph database in plain language

Agents connect to a SQL database, Neo4j or ArangoDB, pull the schema and descriptions into context, write SQL/Cypher/AQL from a question, validate the query before running it (including read-only safety checks), retry on errors and answer from the results.
Database tools: prebuilt per-database toolsets and declarative SQL tools

Connect a database and get ready toolsets (list tables, run SQL, query plans, active queries, locks) or define your own parameterized SQL tools in YAML with auth-bound parameters, served to the agent over MCP.
Home media requests (Sonarr, Radarr, Overseerr, Ombi)

From a chat, search for a movie or show (TheMovieDb), request it from the owner's Sonarr/Radarr/Overseerr/Ombi server with per-user quotas, report issues, and get notified when the download is available.
MQTT edge devices: sensors and actuators as tools
Register IoT/edge devices with a wizard, then the agent lists devices, reads sensor values with history, sends MQTT commands and controls actuators, with device cards and a detail drawer in the UI.
Publish to Chinese social platforms (Xiaohongshu, Douyin, WeChat Channels)
Skills that publish notes and videos to Xiaohongshu, Douyin and WeChat Channels through the user's signed-in creator session (login check and verify first), plus fetching comments and engagement.
Contacts sync across Google, Microsoft, iCloud and CardDAV
One contacts registry with providers for Google, Microsoft, iCloud and any CardDAV server (including IMAP-hosted), so the agent can search and edit the owner's real address books.
Personal life ledger: habits, time logs, plans vs reality, finance

A local database and agent-usable CLI/API for areas, visions, tasks, habits and habit actions, planned events, time logs with templates and daily stats per area, finance snapshots, body measurements and sleep, so the assistant can log what happened and compare it with what was planned.
Provision and rotate scoped service tokens
Creates and rotates narrowly scoped tokens on services such as Vercel and Supabase through their APIs, or by driving the dashboard with Playwright when no API exists.
Charge other agents for work (x402 paywall)

An agent's A2A endpoint can require an x402 payment: middleware issues payment requirements, tracks payment sessions with a nonce store against replay, and runs the task only after a facilitator confirms payment.
Hire a real person for a task

The agent searches people by skill, location or equipment, posts job offers or job-board listings, and manages the hiring lifecycle for things it cannot do itself (QA testing, store beta testing, local errands).
SEO and Search Console analysis skills with CMS write-back

Skills plus scripts that pull Google Search Console and PageSpeed data, detect the site's CMS (WordPress, Ghost, Strapi, Contentful), audit pages, keywords, links and schema, and push approved SEO fixes back to the CMS; companion skills cover Google/Meta/X/LinkedIn/Reddit/TikTok ads with approval boundaries.

The agent asks citation-backed questions of NotebookLM notebooks, adds and reads sources, and generates Studio outputs (audio overview, video, infographic, report, slides, data table) in a chosen language, using the fast internal batchexecute RPC with a browser fallback and rotating across several Google accounts with auto re-auth.
Publish artifacts to the user's own cloud drive

Artifacts are published to one private bucket and one shared CDN distribution in the user's own AWS account, so each later publish is an upload plus invalidation, kept separate from deploy tooling so a site delete can never wipe the drive.
OAuth proxy so MCP clients can sign in through ordinary identity providers

Lets an MCP server accept MCP clients that expect dynamic client registration while authenticating against providers that lack it (GitHub, Google, Azure, Auth0, WorkOS and more), with a consent screen, redirect validation and token handling.
Overleaf sync, compile and marked-up diff

The agent can list, pull, push and two-way sync Overleaf LaTeX projects with conflict detection, compile to PDF, download the .bbl, produce a latexdiff marked-up PDF, and expose all of it as MCP tools or a git remote.
Design systems the agent designs against
Import a design system (from GitHub, shadcn or a brand) into a token contract with evidence and a showcase preview, then have the agent build prototypes, landing pages and slides that follow it.

Checks agent-made slide decks for layout problems (overflow, overlap, off-canvas, crowding) from both the OOXML and rendered images, applies a design policy and writes a review manifest and report before delivery.
Book-length translation projects with EPUB export
Ingest a long work, translate it as a resumable project with consistency across chapters, revise passages, and export to EPUB.
Pixel-verified annotated screenshots and flow recordings

Give a URL and CSS selectors; it captures annotated screenshots, before/after composites, terminal captures and step-by-step flow recordings (GIF/MP4 with cursor, camera and spotlight), placing marks from measured DOM boxes and refusing to save any output that fails pixel validation.
Screenshot library with local AI organizing and search

Captured screenshots are categorized and described by a local Ollama model in the background, embedded for semantic search by description, OCR-transcribed, and can be segmented or upscaled by add-on workers.
From one topic it generates a script, collage keyframes, motion/Ken Burns animation, voice-over, beat-synced music, captions and a thumbnail, then assembles a finished explainer/ad video with ffmpeg.
Animated film from a repo's git history

A skill directs a two-minute animated film from a repository: picks real commits, releases and reverts, builds outline, cast sheet and storyboard in an HTML review studio, then renders a 4K/60fps MP4 after approval.
Agentic footage editing through an edit decision list

The agent analyzes input footage (vision and audio), decides the cuts, writes an edit decision list, and assembles the result with silence trimming, audio mix and loudness normalization, then runs QA and review before delivery.
Dub a video into other languages
Transcribes a video, translates the script, synthesizes a new voiceover per language and re-renders the video with the dubbed audio and captions.

The agent edits a local CapCut/JianYing draft directly (tracks, subtitles, timing, speed, volume, keyframes, effects, templates, TTS, SFX), with lint, dry-run, diff and backup/restore, so the human opens a fully editable project instead of a flattened export.

Plans, drafts, checks quality and revises long documents through a writer IR with numbering and anchors, then exports via Pandoc/LaTeX or publishes to Notion, Feishu, WeChat articles, Obsidian, GitHub or Google Drive.
Long-form fiction pipeline with story state and continuity

Write a novel chapter by chapter with planner, architect, writer, continuity checker, state settler, reviewer and reviser agents; characters, foreshadowing and world facts live in a validated state store and each chapter is drafted in a workspace then committed atomically with its state.
Tailored CV and cover letter PDF generation with page budget

Builds a CV tailored to each posting from a structured career profile into HTML/LaTeX and PDF, keeping experience order, fonts and a page budget, plus generated cover letters and saved application answers.
Editorial SVG diagram skill with geometry verification and diagram import

The agent produces self-contained HTML+SVG diagrams across 42 layout types in light, dark and editorial variants, verified by scripts for label geometry, overlaps and accessibility, and can convert existing draw.io, Excalidraw and Mermaid diagrams into this style.
An infinite whiteboard (shapes, freehand, mind maps, frames, minimap, templates, export) where the agent proposes changes as a patch the owner previews and applies, scoped to a selection.
Train a character LoRA on the user's own images locally (musubi-tuner in a dedicated venv), with presets, install-path checks, progress status and conversion into the image tool's LoRA folder.
Background-refreshed context files about the owner's machine and habits

A context manager keeps a set of Markdown context files up to date in a background worker: host system and resources, GPU compute, storage, devices discovered on the home network, local inventory, recent activity and habits, media profile and browser history, which the assistant reads to ground answers in the real setup.
Import WhatsApp history from exports and phone backups

Parses WhatsApp chat exports and Android/iOS phone backups, extracts per-contact profiles and the best past replies, and bulk-embeds them into the assistant's memory so it starts with years of conversation history.
Memory served as a virtual folder that ordinary file and grep tools read

Hooks intercept the agent's normal Read/Grep/Bash calls on the memory folder and answer them from a SQL-backed store with hybrid lexical and semantic search, so any harness uses memory with its built-in file tools and no extra tool.
Memory-injecting model proxy for outside agents

Point Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode or other agents' base URL at a local proxy; it classifies each request, injects recalled memory into Anthropic or OpenAI-format prompts, and captures turns for extraction, so every agent shares one memory with no plugin.
Structured queries over a markdown note graph

A folder of markdown notes becomes a graph through nesting and inclusion links; agents run database-style queries (frontmatter filters, subtree, graph matches, projections) and retrieve a note with its parent context, and can extract, inline or restructure notes, all on plain files.
Searchable local history of everything on screen and heard

Event-driven capture of screens and audio is turned into OCR and accessibility text, transcripts with speakers, and frames in a local SQLite full-text store with retention and disk-pressure handling; agents search it, get activity summaries and export clips through an MCP server and SDK.
Repo-local agent worklog and handoff kept with the code

A numbered set of reviewable Markdown memory files (overview, architecture, workflow, security, known issues) plus an append-only JSONL agent worklog and a handoff note, regenerated from git changes and validated, so any coding tool can resume where another left off.
Portable single-file memory capsule with WAL, time index and encryption

All memory (text, embeddings, lexical index, time index, metadata) lives in one append-only file with a write-ahead log, crash recovery, as-of-time queries and optional encrypted capsules, so a memory can be copied, shared or backed up as one file.
Per-type reserved budgets for memory recall

Memory recall gives each type of entry (facts, preferences, episodes...) its own token pool retrieved independently, so low-priority types still surface, while behavioral corrections load every time outside the budget competition.
Per-agent private database with self-scheduled next run

Each agent can opt into its own SQLite database that it designs and queries through db_* tools (schema, bulk CSV import/export, soft delete, changelog, storage quota), plus a single schedule_next_run slot so it wakes itself to act on that data; detail tabs show Schema, Data, Views and Activity.

After each exchange the memories that were injected are scored on whether the advice actually worked, either by the main model through a score tool or by an independent sidecar model to avoid self-grading; helpful memories are promoted and bad ones demoted or archived, shaping future recall.

Memory is tiered: an index always in context, a hot set of pinned files plus files ranked by decayed usage frequency preloaded under byte/token/item budgets and recomputed only at model change or compaction, and cold files read by tool.
Keystone memories and trust tiers for shared fleet memory

Owners pin 'keystone' memories that act as policy and always surface, and each agent's writes carry a trust tier that decides how its memories rank and propagate to other agents, with outcome signals (reuse, repeat recall) feeding back into retrieval.
Tree-index reasoning retrieval for long documents

Long PDFs and Markdown files are turned into a table-of-contents style tree (headings detected even without an embedded TOC, with page ranges and summaries); the agent reads the tree and picks the sections to open, giving cited page-level answers with no vector database or chunking.
Scores the agent's memory files out of 100 with critical/warning/info checks (stale daily logs over 30 days, size, config), and builds a prompt asking the agent to clean them up.

Discovers the types and fields already used in a markdown/Obsidian vault, writes a schema, then enforces it on every card, deduplicates entities, fixes wikilinks and orphans, regenerates index (MOC) pages and runs decay cycles that demote untouched cards.
Narrative memory with a routing gate

Each incoming message is routed by a gate to the ongoing narrative (storyline/topic) it continues, or starts a new one; the agent then loads that narrative's continuity summary and events instead of a flat recent history.
Typed schema-driven domain context graph with connectors

You define doc types and their schemas, store entities per schema and link them with free-text edge semantics, extract entities from connectors (e.g. MCP sources), and query/maintain this 'brain' deterministically so agents operate on structured, kept-correct domain data rather than fuzzy recall.
Linked memory notes that update their neighbours on write

Each new memory becomes a note with keywords, tags and a context description; the system finds related past notes, decides which to link, and rewrites the linked notes' context and tags so the memory network evolves as new facts arrive.
Interview agent that builds the owner's profile
An interviewer agent asks the owner questions about themselves, and the answers are transformed and indexed into the memory a personal agent later retrieves to answer as them.
Camera frames and poses are embedded into a spatial vector store so the agent can answer where it saw something and navigate back to a remembered place, with replayable observation streams.
Tiered short/mid/long-term memory with heat-based promotion

An OS-inspired memory manager that keeps short-term, mid-term and long-term stores and promotes/consolidates entries between tiers by access heat and recency, with retrieval and dynamic updating, reaching SOTA on the LoCoMo long-term-memory benchmark.
Hand-editable Markdown memory with cascade re-index

Every memory kind (facts, episodes, profile, agent cases and skills, knowledge pages) lives as Markdown; a watcher and reconciler pick up direct file edits and cascade them into the SQLite and LanceDB indexes, with backfill and per-kind handlers.
Code-grounded memory withheld when its cited paths move

Each memory packet cites repo paths; when those paths move or change, the memory is flagged stale and withheld from recall, a triage command lists what moved and prints the exact reverify or supersede command for a human, and nothing is bulk-cleared automatically.
Encrypted signed knowledge store with expiring agent grants and device sync

Personal records are encrypted and signed in an append-only log that syncs between the owner's devices (hybrid logical clocks, relay) and can be recovered; each agent gets a scoped grant that expires and can be revoked, so it only reads what it was allowed to for as long as allowed.
Session memory shared as a published dataset

Past sessions from several coding agents are scrubbed, indexed and pushed as a dataset; another machine, a teammate or anyone (if public) can recall from it with one flag, and 'ask' answers a question grounded in recalled sessions, naming the sessions used.

Teammates' agents record decisions in parallel into content-addressed event segments synced through the team's own S3 bucket (git experimental); textual merge conflicts cannot happen, and genuine semantic conflicts appear as branches resolved by one new decision.
Proactive recall from every coding agent's history on disk

Indexes sessions already written by 35 agents (including Hermes, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor) with files opened, commands and exit codes and exact edits, then surfaces relevant past work at session start, before an edit and after a failed command; hits note decisions marked rejected or accepted and warn when files touched since have changed. No model or embeddings; 97.2% R@5 on LongMemEval-S.

Probes a configured model and compares its behaviour/fingerprint against a sealed baseline to catch a provider silently swapping or updating the model behind a stable name, so a run can flag that the model is no longer the one that was tested.
Image blob broker: send images to models as stable URLs

Outgoing images get content-hash-keyed, stable, multi-use URLs (local server behind a tunnel or uploads to object storage, drives or image hosts) or provider file uploads, so resent turns stay byte-identical for caching and image tokens are not re-uploaded each turn.
Run your own model on a rented GPU pod

Point it at an SSH-reachable GPU pod (Prime Intellect, Vast.ai, DataCrunch, AWS); it installs vLLM, starts one or more models with GPU memory split across them, tracks them, streams logs and gives an OpenAI-compatible endpoint for the agent.

Saves several Claude Code OAuth logins as credential-only snapshots and, when one hits its limit, activates the next eligible login so the conversation resumes without a hand-over; exhausted logins wait for reset or back-off.
Sign in with many coding-product subscriptions as model sources

Sign-in flows, token refresh and protocol translators that let the owner use accounts from Kiro, Windsurf, Cursor, Qoder, Trae, Zed, CodeBuddy, iFlow, Kimi, Grok CLI, Antigravity, Cline and others as model backends, normalizing streaming, tool calls, thinking and usage.
Free-tier model router with rest periods

Keeps a ranked, refreshed list of free models across OpenRouter, Gemini, Groq, Cerebras and Mistral; each request goes to the smartest one the user has a key for that is awake; rate-limited models rest a minute, daily-capped ones rest until reset, mid-answer failures retry on the next; /free shows awake, resting and no-key models, and paid keys in the shell are ignored.
Prompt-cache expiry countdown and rebuild cost

Shows how long until the provider prompt cache expires for the main agent and each subagent (60 min / 5 min TTLs), detects when a turn rewrote the whole cache and prices that rebuild, so idle-time waste is visible.
VRAM hand-off between chat model and image/video generation

When the local chat model and an image/video pipeline do not both fit in GPU memory, the chat model is unloaded (confirmed gone) before generation and reloaded afterwards in a finally step, with an honest card explaining the wait; chat history is never touched.

Agents and nodes authenticate with decentralized identifiers (DID); middleware verifies DID auth across HTTP, gRPC and connector calls and the SDK signs requests, giving cross-service agent identity without a central token issuer.
Persistent interactive Claude Code session in tmux (subscription-safe)

The project states that headless 'claude -p' runs bill against separate paid Agent SDK credit since 2026-06-15, so it keeps one long-lived interactive claude in a tmux pane, types prompts into it under a cross-process lock, parses replies from the pane, detects stalls by the spinner (not silence) and a watchdog force-recovers a wedged session; a test forbids any 'claude -p' use.
One-click provider switching for installed coding CLIs

Keeps a catalogue of provider presets and writes the chosen one live into each installed CLI's own config (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Hermes, Pi, Grok Build) with backups and project-level patches, plus syncing MCP servers, skills and prompts across them and WebDAV/S3 config sync.
Open-loop follow-ups routed to the best-matching character

Unresolved topics in direct and group chats are tracked as open loops; a scheduler scores candidate characters (domain match, relationship, recent-recommendation penalties, relevance threshold) and sends a follow-up recommendation introducing the right one.
Need discovery proposes new specialist characters

On a short interval and daily, recent conversation signals are scanned for needs no existing character covers; above a confidence threshold a new specialist role is generated and offered to the owner as a friend request, with daily limits, suppression windows, expiry and opt-outs for medical, legal and finance.
Trust policies for incoming agent calls

Markdown trust policies (open, careful, strict) with YAML front matter decide who may call your agent: zero-token allow/deny lists for admins, contacts and blocked keys, onboarding strangers by invite code or payment, and an LLM trust agent only for the 'ask' case; every request must still be signed.
Send each errand to the best-value installed harness, with skills and a cost receipt

Detects which coding CLIs, subscriptions and model credits are installed (Claude, Codex, Cursor, Devin, Copilot, Cline, OpenRouter, local), picks the cheapest capable lane per job, stages the needed skill bundles for the delegate, can ask a panel of stronger models for a second opinion, and reports what each job cost.
Repo Mesh: pull-based task queue across your machines

Tasks with dependencies go into a queue bound to one repository; idle machines on a peer mesh claim them into fresh worktrees by capability tags and free slots, with spawn budgets, duplicate-dispatch guards, dependency-failure notices and idle-session reaping.
Cross-person agent hotline with three-state delivery

Two people's agents on different machines talk directly over the owner's own network with a shared secret; send reports sent, delivered-to-process and answered as separate states, and a check tool shows a message nobody picked up.
HTTP chat API over any terminal coding agent by screen parsing

Runs a TUI agent in a virtual terminal, diffs screen snapshots to extract the agent's messages, strips each agent's input box and chrome, detects readiness, and serves send/messages/events (SSE) plus a web chat.
Live messaging and file claims between coding harnesses

One local MCP server lets Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI sessions see who is present, claim files and get overlap warnings before editing, message each other live through a relay, and hand off tasks with a written handoff and review packet.
Staff a task team from a large library of specialist agents

A router matches the task against hundreds of local and hub specialist agent cards (A2A cards, linted and migrated), shows the model a compressed candidate shortlist to cut routing tokens, and spins up a temporary orchestrator that calls the chosen specialists, with approvals, receipts and a run journal.

Bots, humans and webhooks are all actors with persistent inboxes in shared threads; unaddressed messages go to the thread default bot, only the first @mention in a reply wakes the next bot, a hop limit stops loops, and a hand-off is held until the target bot has caught up on newer thread messages.
Magentic manager orchestration with plan review and stall intervention

A manager-led orchestration where a lead keeps a task/plan ledger, reviews progress each round, can pause for human plan-review, and detects and intervenes when the team stalls or loops - a distinct pattern beyond simple handoffs or chains.

One agent session can read the text on any other terminal tab, type into it, open new tabs and start agents, keep a group chat and task list with reports that survive restarts, and be told how long each tab has been idle.
Auction swarm: agents bid for tasks
Tasks are put up for auction; agents submit bids (custom scoring) and the winning agent does the work, also in batches.
Hook-based message bus between different coding CLIs

Launching any of 11 coding CLIs through hcom installs per-tool hooks that log activity to SQLite and deliver messages mid-turn or wake idle agents, so agents can message each other, read each other's transcripts, file edits and terminal screens, subscribe to status/edit-collision events, and spawn, fork, resume or kill each other in real terminals.
Supervisor team of mixed-vendor coding CLIs with durable handoff and inbox

A supervisor CLI (e.g. Claude Code) gets MCP tools to assign work to, hand off to (and wait on), or message worker CLIs from other vendors (Codex, Kiro, Copilot, Cursor, OpenCode, Kimi, Hermes...), each running with its own login in its own terminal; worker status is read from its terminal, messages queue in an inbox until the recipient is idle, and handoff results survive restarts.
tmux-compatible remote daemon for agent teammates

A Go daemon speaks enough tmux (split, list, wait-for) over a WebSocket PTY that agents expecting tmux (Claude Code teammates, Codex teams) spawn as native panes; Claude hooks are routed back for notifications.
Tower: lead agent running file-scoped missions for worker sessions

A lead plans missions with task checklists and reserved file scopes, spawns worker sessions on their own branches, and receives findings and inbox messages; a mission cannot be marked completed with open tasks, no diff, or unread messages, a non-clean review sends it back, and only the lead merges or abandons, all kept in a git-backed store.
Always-on goal-driven operator agent with server-paced wake loop

One long-running agent plans from a goal, posts jobs, reviews results and merges PRs, keeping its charter, plan and memory in a git repo; the server wakes it every 3-30 minutes only when it is idle and the owner is not typing to it.
Which agent needs you: attention ranking and narration
Ranks all running agent sessions by how urgently they need the user (waiting for approval, finished, stuck) and can speak a short summary of what needs attention.
Single-active lease per task across agent runtimes

A task (Work) holds one active lease naming which agent runtime and attempt owns it, with a recovery-pending state and deadline, so two agents (e.g. Codex and Claude) never work the same task at once and a crashed owner is recovered rather than duplicated.
Manager agent answers workers' permission dialogs

Workers' PermissionRequest hook posts each permission ask to the server, which types it into the manager agent's terminal; the manager allows or denies, and any silence, timeout or error falls back to the normal dialog for a person.
Agents that are not reachable directly register a mailbox; messages to them are held by a relay and delivered when the agent comes back online, with endpoint resolution by address.
Cross-repo ticket DAG with per-repo routing

A request is decomposed into tickets with a dependency graph and an assigned repo alias; a scheduler runs them in order across repositories, routes each to that repo's admin agent and tracks cost per ticket.
Independent review gate on agent-claimed tasks

An agent claims a task with its bound runtime session recorded as provenance; submitted work can only be accepted or rejected by an authorized actor other than the assignee, and a rejected review continues the same task.
Deferred tasks that wake on other tasks or a deadline

A task can be parked to wake when all or any of a set of watched tasks reach an outcome, or when a deadline passes, so a lead can wait for helpers without polling; waits survive restarts and stale ones are reaped.
Wave planner with critical path and runway warning

A planned task DAG is validated and split into parallel waves, the critical path is computed and shown, dispatch auto-advances as waves finish under a concurrency cap, and a runway indicator warns before the ready queue empties at current fleet speed.
Racing experiment forks with a safe fallback

When an assistant faces a choice, candidate answers run as isolated forked sessions or worktrees in parallel; the first to complete wins and its answer is replayed onto the original session, and if all fail the most rollback-safe candidate is used.
Branches and selective synthesis into a decision brief

A question branches to several specialists in parallel; a human selects or excludes each output, and the room publishes an immutable decision brief whose evidence and provenance (which model, which output) stay linked.
Hire outside agents over Nostr with paid jobs

Agents publish capability cards to Nostr relays; other agents discover them, send jobs, get results and pay in SOL with on-chain verification, spend ceilings, delegation proofs, a job ledger with recovery and reputation, exposed as MCP tools.
LLM council: draft, vote, pick winner, refine (TypeScript)

Several council member models each draft a plan or document, members vote on the drafts with quorum rules, a winner is selected and a refiner merges the best parts; sessions can be stopped cleanly per owner.
Collaborative build DAG with a single-writer lease

Several models propose, a coordinator delegates a dependency graph of work, and only the agent holding the writer lease may edit the shared folder at a time, with a gate script and validator between rounds.
Capability search over a registry of outside agents with nested teams

Agents on different machines register their capabilities with a hub; an agent facing a task searches the registry semantically for teammates, invites them into a group chat, and sub-groups can form for subtasks with async task tracking.

Two people's assistants negotiate a meeting over A2A: one proposes slots, the other counter-proposes against its owner's calendar and working hours until a slot free for both is found, with a shared thread id, a hard hop cap, a daily outbound-call budget and a booking audit.
Characters post to a social feed (moments)

Each AI character posts moments with images and music themes; an editorial planner rotates content angles so characters differ day to day, an image budget caps generation spend, and the owner can like and comment.
The full orchestrator - classifier routing, agents, MCP tools, realtime voice and tracing - runs entirely on iPhone/iPad/Mac with no server.
Wasted-context report and learned read shield

Tracks every file read and whether it was later used, prices sessions per model segment, shows heatmaps and an efficiency score, learns which files are usually useless per project and can warn on or block those reads via a .contextignore.
Trust stamps carried inside agent-made files

Agents stamp files they produce or verify with compact claims (trust score, source, evidence, AI-made, verified), embedded in the file itself (Markdown, DOCX, PDF, images, spreadsheets and more) or a sidecar, optionally signed; the next agent runs a check and builds on verified claims instead of re-verifying.
Which session is burning your plan quota (session runway)
Attributes live Codex and Claude token use to individual sessions against the 5-hour and weekly windows, with API-equivalent price per session and a pace estimate for the week.
Pause, edit and forward model requests (request interception)

Turn on interception for a session and each outgoing model request is held in the dashboard, where the owner can inspect and edit the payload and then approve it (or let it time out) before it reaches the provider; edits are summarised and reflected in the log.
System prompt history and diff across versions
Captures the system prompt each agent version actually sends, keeps its history and shows what changed between versions in the dashboard, next to a workflow timeline of calls.
Tape trace inspector and model-view replay

Every session is an append-only tape of facts (messages, provider attempts, tool surfaces, view manifests); a trace inspector shows each request and can rebuild exactly what the model saw for any past call, with lineage across compaction.
Spend burn-rate forecast to month end
Fits the last 7 days of spend with linear regression and smoothing to project month-end cost and days until the budget limit is reached.
Costs page that prices scheduled-job runs, flags token anomalies, shows week-over-week change and cache savings, and produces an optimization score with concrete suggestions.
Unified usage history across other coding CLIs, kept after they delete it

Parses the session logs of Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, Qwen Code, OpenCode, Pi, Antigravity and Grok into one normalized, priced history with daily/weekly/monthly, per-model and per-project views, cached so the history survives after those tools delete their own files, with shareable text/SVG reports.
Verify a run record and check whether it reproduces

Each run leaves a hash-chained trace with receipts and evidence; trace verify checks the record was not altered, and trace reproduce compares the recorded journal with a fresh run of the same workflow and classifies every task by why it did or did not reproduce, with lineage and an OpenTelemetry export.
Live reasoning map the agent maintains

Through MCP tools the agent keeps a revisioned graph of goals, hypotheses with confidence, options scored per criterion, experiments, evidence and supports/challenges links, with sources; the user can edit it and their edits are protected from the agent.
Agent process and resource usage window
Scans and samples CPU/memory of every agent child process (Codex, Claude Code) across the process tree and shows it in a resource window.
Config layer map and skill/hook/MCP dependency graph

Shows every skill, command, agent and hook from user, project and plugin sources with which one overrides which, maps how hooks, skills, commands and MCP servers depend on each other as numbered chains, and extracts each skill's trigger keywords with example prompts that would fire it.
Scoped spend budgets with incidents and auto-pause

Monthly spend budgets per company, agent or project with soft-warning and hard-stop thresholds; crossing one opens a budget incident, pauses the scope and cancels its running work until the owner resolves it, with a costs page and provider quota windows.

Writes a complete runtime (portable Node, built daemon and start scripts for macOS, Linux and Windows) onto a USB stick with AES and HMAC keys in its config, and detects and verifies the stick when plugged in.
Run the assistant's scheduled skills on GitHub Actions with no machine on

A scheduler workflow on GitHub Actions cron dispatches skills and chained skill runs on free CI runners using a chosen coding CLI, keeps memory and outputs committed in the repo, sends results by Telegram, and audits network egress of each run.
Encrypted file transfer between your machines (direct peer, server fallback)
Files and workspace folders move between registered machines in encrypted chunks, trying a direct peer connection first and falling back to a server-routed path with size limits and route caching.
Detached dispatch of jobs to another host

Send a durable job (workspace, session, model, permission policy) to another machine running the app; the target provisions its runtime and syncs model config, keeps running if the controller disconnects, keeps a reconnectable transcript, and permission requests can be answered remotely.
Detect, install and update other agent CLIs from a catalog

An embedded, refreshable catalog of 109 agent CLIs with detection strategies (binary, npm, pip, brew) and installers per package manager, checking versions in parallel and offering updates, exposed over CLI, TUI, tray, REST and gRPC.

The agent never mutates infrastructure itself: it submits a JSON intent that a deterministic controller validates against a five-action allowlist and a generation guard before applying; known problems (e.g. OOM) are fixed by rules, novel ones escalate to a companion agent whose proposal needs human approval in Slack.
Deploy apps to the owner's own servers from a typed intent

A typed config says which servers the owner has and which apps they want; the tool resolves it into a desired-state graph and plans, applies and prunes real infrastructure (hosts over SSH, Cloudflare, Forgejo, Komodo, GitHub) with locks, migrations and backups.
Distributed runner fleet with heartbeat liveness and restart

Agent runners run across the owner's own machines as pods that send batched heartbeats; the control plane tracks liveness, detects stalled/dead runners and restarts execution, with isolated per-agent block-store workspaces, all steered from one console.
Each agent workspace can join its own Tailscale or NetBird overlay network through a managed sidecar, so an agent's computer reaches private hosts without exposing the main app.

After a config change (for example a new model id), the agent's health endpoint is probed; K failures in M minutes restore the last config that was seen healthy, restart the service and alert by Telegram/Slack/Discord/webhook.
TLA+ models of agent runtime protocols checked in CI

Compaction, delegated turns, file locks, message queue, task and workspace lifecycles, workspace leases, history crash recovery and async primitives are specified in TLA+ and model-checked by a CI workflow, catching races before they ship.
Config releases: run the approved config, not the session's copy

Agent sessions load agents, skills and runtime config from a read-only, built release of the base branch rather than their own working checkout; a release can be quarantined, and runtimes swap or reload it in place, so an agent editing its own config cannot change what is running until it is merged.
Plugin facets across processes with replicated state

Plugins declare services they provide and need; each plugin splits into facets that load in the right place (agent worker, terminal UI, web UI), services keep stable facades across reconnects, and authoritative state replicates to local and remote consumers as atomic delta transactions.

Answer questions over very long documents by splitting them into chunks, letting member agents answer from each chunk in parallel, then retrieving and summarizing the useful partial answers into one reply.

The owner defines named prompt transformations (summary, key insights, questions and custom ones), tries them in a playground, and applies them to any added source so each document gets stored, searchable insight notes.
Autonomous data discovery with refuter-verified insights

Pointed at a warehouse (BigQuery, Snowflake, Postgres and others), the agent learns the schema, picks what to investigate within a query budget, writes and fixes SQL, then a separate verifier and refuter re-query every claimed number before an insight and ranked recommendation is shown.
Crawls a site and writes an llms.txt (and full variant) summarising its pages so an agent can load a compact map of the site.
Social-media crawler cluster for opinion data

A crawler subsystem (MindSpider) scrapes posts and user comments across Weibo, Xiaohongshu, Douyin, Kuaishou and other platforms, with broad-topic extraction and deep sentiment crawling, feeding an analysis pipeline.

The agent supplies a JSON schema and the tool extracts every matching data point from a large set of documents in chunks, returning structured rows as a file instead of reading everything into context.
Numbers traced back to the code output that produced them

Every numeric value in the written text must reference a value in the analysis code's outputs; values are checked against those outputs and rendered as links back to their source, so a reader can verify each number.
Adaptive tutor that plans lessons from your feedback

Builds a syllabus for any topic, delivers one lesson at a time, reads the learner's annotations and feedback to shape the next lesson, then evaluates and summarizes, with learning-method skills (Feynman, deep, graph).
Citation and quote-fidelity verification against source documents

Every finding's quote is matched against the extracted source text; on top of fuzzy matching, a deterministic guard checks salient tokens (amounts, durations, percentages, negation) so a quote that changes '90 days' to '30 days' or drops a 'not' is rejected as fabricated.

From a scenario or document, generates demographically grounded persona agents, runs them on a simulated social feed and an AMM prediction market over rounds, then reports the outcome distribution, counterfactuals and a written report.
Multi-analyst stock research with bull/bear and risk debates

For one stock, market, sector, fundamentals and news analyst agents write reports, bull and bear researchers debate them, a research manager decides, a trader proposes a position and aggressive/neutral/conservative risk agents debate it before a final view, at selectable depth.
Runs the crawler locally: sitemap discovery, crawl scope and regex rules, depth limits, robots handling, canonical URLs, relevance-ranked site maps and HTML-to-Markdown, without a hosted API key.
Given a URL, extracts the site's logo, color roles, fonts and brand marks into a structured brand profile, with an LLM pass that falls back safely when the model fails.
Graph-based web exploration with adversarial answer synthesis

Research runs crawl pages as nodes of a growing knowledge graph, choose the next link by reasoning over the graph, then write several drafts that are attacked and revised before the final answer; the web UI streams the live graph.

Researches a topic over the last 30 days by fanning out to Reddit, X, YouTube transcripts, TikTok, HN, Polymarket odds, GitHub, Bluesky and more in parallel, then dedupes, clusters, reranks by real engagement and writes a grounded brief (optionally an HTML page).
Scholarly and filings source providers (PubMed, ClinicalTrials, EDGAR, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar)

Typed research providers query PubMed, ClinicalTrials.gov, SEC EDGAR filings, OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar, arXiv and Wikipedia directly, normalizing results into citable source documents, with robots.txt checks and an SSRF-safe fetcher.

Typed tools fetch income statements, balance sheets, cash flows, key ratios, segments, earnings, SEC filings (and read them), insider trades, institutional holdings, news and stock screens for a ticker, so the agent can research a company from primary data (informational only, not advice).
Citation DOI cross-verification across scholarly databases
Every printed citation is looked up in CrossRef, OpenAlex and Semantic Scholar and kept only when its DOI appears in at least two of them, so drafts carry no invented references.
Claim labels in research reports: verified with source, inferred, missing

Every claim in a research report carries [VERIFIED:url], [INFERRED] or [MISSING]; verified labels must point at a collected source, synthesis may not upgrade inferred or missing claims, and the report shows counts of each so the reader sees what is actually known.
Per-platform backend routing with a health doctor

Each platform has a preferred and fallback access route (CLI tool, API, MCP or scraper); a doctor probes every route, reports what works and how to fix the rest, and the project swaps a route when a site blocks it without the owner changing anything.
Job portal scanners across ~100 ATS providers with liveness checks

Scans job boards directly through ATS APIs and pages (Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workday and ~100 more) with SSRF/IP guards, then checks each posting is still open through API, page and browser fallbacks before it is evaluated.
Prediction-market odds and public data feeds

Ask 'what are the odds of X' and the agent searches a unified market index across Polymarket, Kalshi, Manifold, Metaculus, PredictIt, Betfair and Smarkets, plus FRED economic series and ACLED conflict events, with freshness tracking.
Autoresearch: agent population improves a graded task

Give a codebase and a grader; several coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) work in isolated workspaces, every commit is scored by a sealed grader the agents cannot read, and they share attempts, notes and skills through a hub, optionally split into islands with migration, until an auto-stop rule fires.
While answering, the search agent decides whether a quick card applies and shows it next to the answer: stock quote with chart, calculation result or weather, each fetched by its own widget executor.

A runtime proxy and watcher that intercepts a deployed agent's model/tool traffic, evaluates the live trajectory with a trained safety model, and intervenes (blocks or flags) unsafe steps, exposed as a server, CLI and websocket proxy.
Context trust scores with provenance filtering and decay

Every piece of prompt context carries its provenance and a trust score (CLI 0.95, chat apps 0.70-0.75, web fetch 0.50, memory 0.70...); summaries and old history decay in trust, and a filter drops parts below a minimum trust or from blocked provenances before the model call, logging each exclusion.
Backup before approved destructive file changes

Before the agent deletes or overwrites files, the approval names the exact change and a recoverable copy goes to a bounded backup vault with a receipt; if backups are off or space runs out the prompt says plainly that the change may be unrecoverable.
Edit gate that catches an AI change removing an auth guard

Compiles the backend's routes, guards, queries and side effects into a deterministic behavior graph, arms a baseline, then after each agent edit diffs the graph and blocks the edit (via a PostToolUse hook) if a route lost its guard, became newly exposed or broke an invariant; offline, no model calls.
Per-project agent VM with host-held keys

Each project gets its own pre-provisioned VM where agents can run with full autonomy; git signing and push go through a forwarded SSH agent so private keys never enter the VM, and secrets are rendered into tmpfs that disappears on reboot.
Agent writes as reviewable change requests with field-level diffs

Every agent write to shared data or docs is packaged as a change request carrying a message, author and per-operation field-level diff; a person reviews, revises individual operations, and merges or rejects, with workspace rules deciding what auto-merges.
Agent BOM and cryptographic seal with verify

Takes a cryptographic snapshot (seal) of an agent's whole definition and emits an AI-BOM (CycloneDX) listing its models, tools, prompts and MCP servers, then can verify later that the running agent matches the sealed one.

When an agent runs npm/pip (and other) installs, the requested packages are identified and evaluated for malicious or risky signs before the install runs, blocking or asking, with a repair step for already-installed bad packages.
Task scope contract enforced on every tool call

Each task gets a confirmed contract (review-only or edit, allowed paths, a budget for spawning helper agents); a guard on tool calls denies writes outside it, extra delegation or repeated re-checks, and explains why with a suggested next step, in watch or enforce levels.

A periodic job compares each agent's last hour against its 7-day baseline and raises deduplicated alerts for risk spikes, never-seen actions, call-frequency spikes and cost spikes, using plain counts over the audit log.
Agent profiles that hide paths and gate commands, with a scriptable policy

A profile sets allow, ask or deny per command and CLI, and hide or show per file or folder so hidden paths are absent from what the agent sees; a policy script and built-ins (mount-root guard, output cap) gate every filesystem op and session write before it runs.
Runtime threat monitor that pauses or kills the agent's sandbox

A daemon watches the agent container's processes, network connections, files, logs and cgroup usage, matches them against Sigma rules and GTFOBins patterns, records evidence, and automatically pauses or kills the container when it sees something dangerous.
Formal prover for sandbox policy changes

Before a policy change is applied, a prover compares the candidate against the current boundary and lists any new reach it grants (a new host with credentials, a new API method, process or write access), so only widening changes wait for human review.
Sandbox learning mode writes least-privilege profiles

Run an agent once in learning mode; its file access is traced (strace on Linux, eslogger on macOS) and collapsed into a least-privilege filesystem profile that auto-loads next time, with drift detection that prompts before widening a profile later.
Kernel-enforced agent policies that follow process lineage

A YAML/DSL policy compiles to eBPF rules that kill forbidden actions anywhere under the agent's process tree (e.g. no git push, no writes outside /src, even via scripts), enforce causal order such as tests before commit, and only notify when outputs go stale; the kill reason is fed back to the agent through hooks or MCP.
API-method-level egress rules (HTTP, GraphQL, JSON-RPC, MCP)

The sandbox egress proxy enforces rules at the request level, not only by domain: allow or deny by HTTP method and path, GraphQL operation, JSON-RPC/MCP method or websocket, with live policy updates and token-grant injection per endpoint.
Per-service egress policy presets with provenance

Ready-made network policy presets per service (GitHub, Gmail, Outlook, Jira, npm, PyPI, Hugging Face, Brave, Tavily, local inference...) that are added or removed as a unit, with recorded provenance and ownership, fail-closed removal and a readable scope summary.

When a sandboxed command is denied, the failure is attributed to a file path or network host and the user gets a card proposing the narrowest sensible grant (nearest directory, never the home or workspace root); accepted grants are stored and reused.
Page sanitizer against hidden prompt injection and data leaks

Before a page reaches the model, rules strip hidden text, HTML comments, invisible Unicode, meta/attribute/JSON-LD injection, encoded payloads and known injection phrases, redact cross-origin frames and user comments, and mask PII and secrets.

In strict mode the agent may only send pre-approved response templates (with fields filled from context); generation picks and fills a template instead of writing free text, so wording stays compliant.
Flags retrieved chunks or user input that are padded, oversized or repetitively structured to make the model forget its system prompt or exhaust the token budget, on input and retrieval paths.
Automated red-teaming of your own agent

Generates attacks against the owner's agent with plugins (indirect prompt injection, excessive agency, tool discovery, SSRF, data leaks and many more) and multi-turn strategies (iterative, Crescendo, GOAT), grades the responses and reports which attacks succeeded.
Injection scanning of images, QR codes, PDFs, audio and video

Before untrusted files reach the agent, text is extracted from PDFs, images (OCR), QR codes, audio and video and run through the injection pattern set, and the report says what could not be read so a clean result is not mistaken for a full scan.
Exfiltration detection in inline code plus project taint

Shell commands and inline interpreter code in 15+ languages (python -c, node -e, PowerShell and more) are parsed for reads of secrets flowing to the network, including obfuscation; once untrusted content is read the project is marked tainted with its source so later risky calls are blocked.

An input rail checks each user message against the configured allowed and disallowed topics and blocks or redirects off-topic requests before the main model answers, composable in order with jailbreak and content-safety rails.
Before a resource is fetched, a gateway plugin checks its URL, domain and IP against VirusTotal (with a small cache and optional submission of unknown URLs) and blocks known-malicious ones.
